10	/-!
11	# Conditional assembly kit for affine divisor representability
12	
13	This file isolates the formal tail between a chart-wise universal certified family and
14	the affine equivalence of DDR-9.F6.  It deliberately makes the remaining F5 hypotheses
15	explicit:

128	    (U : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),

131	    (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J)
132	    (i' : (glueData k g r1).J) (j' : (glueData k g r2).J)
133	    (omega : ChartRing i j →ₐ[k] S) (omega' : ChartRing i' j' →ₐ[k] S),

135	        = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom omega'.toRingHom) ≫ ChartMap i' j' →

143	    (U : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),
144	      CertifiedDivisorFamily C (ChartRing i j) pi g)
145	    (hU : IsCompatible (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U)
146	    {S : Type u} [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
147	    (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J)
148	    (i' : (glueData k g r1).J) (j' : (glueData k g r2).J)
149	    (omega : ChartRing i j →ₐ[k] S) (omega' : ChartRing i' j' →ₐ[k] S)

156	    divRepPullAt (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U i j omega
157	      = divRepPullAt (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U i' j' omega' :=

164	/-- The exact output expected from F5 before the affine equivalence is packaged.
165	`isDivRepClassify_pull` is the hom-side law in the refinement-stable clause spelling;
166	classifier uniqueness turns it into the second inverse law automatically. -/
167	structure DivRepAffinePullback where
168	  pull : ∀ (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S],
169	    (overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver) → DivFamZar C S pi g
170	  pull_classify : ∀ (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
171	    (F : DivFamZar C S pi g),
172	    pull S (divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 S F) = F
173	  isDivRepClassify_pull : ∀ (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
174	    (v : overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver),
175	    IsDivRepClassify hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 (pull S v) v.left
176	  pull_naturality : ∀ {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
177	    [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] (phi : A →ₐ[k] B) (v : overSpec k A ⟶ DivOver),
178	    pull B (Over.overSpecMap phi ≫ v) = DivFamZar.mapAlgHom phi (pull A v)
179	
180	namespace DivRepAffinePullback
181	
182	/-- The affine representability equivalence assembled from an F5 pullback package.
183	The inverse is the landed backward classifier; its hom-side inverse law follows from
184	`divRepClassifyZar_eq_of_isDivRepClassify`. -/
185	noncomputable def equiv
186	    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
187	    (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] :
188	    (overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver) ≃ DivFamZar C S pi g where
189	  toFun := D.pull S
190	  invFun := divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 S
191	  left_inv v :=
192	    (divRepClassifyZar_eq_of_isDivRepClassify hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2
193	      (D.pull S v) v (D.isDivRepClassify_pull S v)).symm
194	  right_inv := D.pull_classify S
195	
196	@[simp]
197	theorem equiv_apply
198	    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
199	    (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] (v : overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver) :
200	    equiv (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2)
201	        (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D S v = D.pull S v :=
202	  rfl
203	
204	@[simp]
205	theorem equiv_symm_apply
206	    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
207	    (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] (F : DivFamZar C S pi g) :
208	    (equiv (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2)
209	      (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D S).symm F
210	      = divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 S F :=
211	  rfl
212	
213	/-- Naturality of the assembled affine equivalence, in the frozen DDR-9 spelling. -/
214	theorem equiv_naturality
215	    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
216	    {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
217	    [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] (phi : A →ₐ[k] B)
218	    (v : overSpec k A ⟶ DivOver) :
219	    equiv (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2)
220	        (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D B (Over.overSpecMap phi ≫ v)
221	      = DivFamZar.mapAlgHom phi
222	          (equiv (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2)
223	            (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D A v) :=
224	  D.pull_naturality phi v

\begin{definition}[Sections of the divisor sheaf]
  \label{def:divisorSections}
  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.divisorSections}
  \uses{def:scheme_ord, lem:ord_functionFieldOverAlgebraMap_le_one, def:curveDivisor,
    def:functionFieldOverAlgebraMap}
  \leanok
  \source{papaioannou-algebraic-rr:page-0007}
  For a Weil divisor \(D\) and a nonempty open \(U\), the sections of \(\mathcal O(D)\) over \(U\)
  are
  \[
    \mathcal O(D)(U) = \{ g \in K(X) : \text{at every closed point } x \in U,\ g \text{ has pole
      order} \le D_x \},
  \]
  the rational functions with poles bounded by \(D\) on \(U\); over the empty open the sections are
  the zero module (forced by the sheaf condition, since the empty sieve covers \(\bot\)). This is a
  \(K\)-submodule of \(K(X)\): it contains \(0\); it is closed under addition because a valuation is
  subadditive, \(\mathrm{ord}_x(g_1 + g_2) \ge \min(\mathrm{ord}_x g_1, \mathrm{ord}_x g_2)\), so
  the pole bound is preserved; and closed under \(K\)-scaling because constants have no poles
  (\ref{lem:ord_functionFieldOverAlgebraMap_le_one}).
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Nonempty opens of an irreducible space meet]
  \label{lem:opens_inf_nonempty}

  being the unit \(u\). The stalk \(\struct{Y,x}\) is a discrete valuation ring (\ref{def:scheme_ord}),

\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[The fibre Weil divisor]
  \label{def:fiberWeilDivisor}
  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.fiberWeilDivisor, AlgebraicGeometry.fiberWeilDivisor_nonneg,
    AlgebraicGeometry.fiberWeilDivisor_coeffAt_of_mem_chart₁,
    AlgebraicGeometry.fiberWeilDivisor_coeffAt_of_mem_chart₀,
    AlgebraicGeometry.fiberWeilDivisor_deg_nonneg,
    AlgebraicGeometry.fiberWeilDivisor_ne_zero_of_notMem_chart₁,
    AlgebraicGeometry.fiberWeilDivisor_deg_pos_of_notMem_chart₁}
  \uses{thm:fiberCoordUnit_order, def:divOf, def:curveDivisor, def:curveDivisor_deg,
    thm:residueDeg_pos}
  \leanok
  The \emph{fibre Weil divisor} \(F\) is the effective part of \(\mathrm{div}(u)\): the Weil divisor
  (\ref{def:curveDivisor}) with coefficient \(F_x = \max(\mathrm{ord}_x(u), 0)\) at each closed point
  \(x\). It is effective (\(F \ge 0\)); it vanishes on \(V_1\) (\(F_x = 0\) for \(x \in V_1\)); it
  agrees with \(\mathrm{div}(u)\) on \(V_0\) (\(F_x = \mathrm{ord}_x(u)\) for \(x \in V_0\)); and its
  degree is nonnegative. If moreover some closed point \(x_0 \in V_0\) lies outside \(V_1\) --- a
  point of the fibre over \([1 : 0]\) --- then \(F\) is nonzero and has strictly positive degree.
\end{definition}
\begin{proof}
  \leanok
  Effectivity is immediate from \(F_x = \max(\mathrm{ord}_x(u), 0) \ge 0\). On \(V_1\) one has
  \(\mathrm{ord}_x(u) \le 0\) (\ref{thm:fiberCoordUnit_order}), so \(F_x = \max(\mathrm{ord}_x(u), 0)
  = 0\); on \(V_0\) one has \(\mathrm{ord}_x(u) \ge 0\), so \(F_x = \mathrm{ord}_x(u)\). The degree
  \(\deg_K F = \sum_x F_x\,[\kappa(x):K]\) (\ref{def:curveDivisor_deg}) is a finite sum of
  nonnegative terms, each \(F_x \ge 0\) and each residue degree nonnegative, hence \(\deg_K F \ge 0\).
  Given a witness \(x_0 \in V_0 \setminus V_1\): there \(F_{x_0} = \mathrm{ord}_{x_0}(u) \ge 1\)
  (\ref{thm:fiberCoordUnit_order}), so \(F \ne 0\); and the degree, again a sum of nonnegative terms,
  is bounded below by the single term \(F_{x_0}\,[\kappa(x_0):K] \ge 1\cdot[\kappa(x_0):K] > 0\),
  using positivity of the residue degree (\ref{thm:residueDeg_pos}). Hence \(\deg_K F > 0\).
\end{proof}

\section{The twist lattices on the two-cover}

Fix a Weil divisor \(D\) on \(Y\). The twisted divisors \(D + nF\) have divisor sheaves whose
sections over the two charts and their overlap are \(K\)-submodules of the function field \(K(Y)\).
We record how these section lattices vary with \(n\): fixed over \(V_1\) and over the overlap,
growing over \(V_0\); from this the two-cover denominator lattices form an increasing chain that
exhausts the fixed overlap module \(N = \struct Y(D)(V_0 \cap V_1)\), by clearing poles at the
finite fibre over \([1 : 0]\).

74	theorem LinearMap.injective_of_surjective_of_rankAtStalk_eq
75	    {M N : Type u} [AddCommGroup M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module R M] [Module R N]
76	    [Module.Finite R M] [Module.Projective R M] [Module.Projective R N]
77	    (φ : M →ₗ[R] N) (hsurj : Function.Surjective φ)
78	    (hrank : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R,
79	      Module.rankAtStalk M p = Module.rankAtStalk N p) :
80	    Function.Injective φ := by
81	  -- a right inverse of `φ` (the projective lifting), and the induced splitting
82	  obtain ⟨l, hl⟩ := φ.exists_rightInverse_of_surjective (LinearMap.range_eq_top.mpr hsurj)
83	  obtain ⟨e, he₁, -⟩ := (LinearMap.exact_subtype_ker_map φ).splitSurjectiveEquiv
84	    (Submodule.injective_subtype (LinearMap.ker φ)) ⟨l, hl⟩
85	  -- the kernel is a finite projective direct summand
86	  haveI : Module.Finite R N := Module.Finite.of_surjective φ hsurj
87	  haveI : Module.Finite R ↥(LinearMap.ker φ) :=
88	    Module.Finite.of_surjective
89	      (LinearMap.fst R ↥(LinearMap.ker φ) N ∘ₗ e.toLinearMap)
90	      (Prod.fst_surjective.comp e.surjective)
91	  haveI : Module.Projective R ↥(LinearMap.ker φ) :=
92	    Module.Projective.of_split (LinearMap.ker φ).subtype
93	      (LinearMap.fst R ↥(LinearMap.ker φ) N ∘ₗ e.toLinearMap)
94	      (LinearMap.ext fun x => by
95	        have hx := LinearMap.congr_fun he₁ x
96	        simp only [LinearMap.coe_comp, LinearEquiv.coe_coe, Function.comp_apply] at hx ⊢
97	        rw [hx, e.apply_symm_apply]
98	        rfl)
99	  -- the kernel has rank zero at every stalk
100	  have hker : Module.rankAtStalk (R := R) ↥(LinearMap.ker φ) = 0 := by
101	    funext p
102	    have h1 := congrFun (Module.rankAtStalk_eq_of_equiv e) p
103	    have h2 := congrFun (Module.rankAtStalk_prod (R := R) ↥(LinearMap.ker φ) N) p
104	    rw [Pi.add_apply] at h2
105	    have h3 := hrank p
106	    rw [Pi.zero_apply]
107	    omega
108	  haveI : Subsingleton ↥(LinearMap.ker φ) :=
109	    Module.rankAtStalk_eq_zero_iff_subsingleton.mp hker
110	  exact LinearMap.ker_eq_bot.mp (Submodule.eq_bot_of_subsingleton)
111	
112	/-- **Nested submodules with same-rank finite projective quotients are equal**: the
113	canonical surjection `M ⧸ K₁ → M ⧸ K₂` is injective by the rank engine, so the larger
114	submodule collapses onto the smaller. -/
115	theorem Submodule.eq_of_le_of_rankAtStalk_quotient_eq
116	    {M : Type u} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] {K₁ K₂ : Submodule R M} (hle : K₁ ≤ K₂)
117	    [Module.Finite R (M ⧸ K₁)] [Module.Projective R (M ⧸ K₁)]
118	    [Module.Projective R (M ⧸ K₂)]
119	    (hrank : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R,
120	      Module.rankAtStalk (M ⧸ K₁) p = Module.rankAtStalk (M ⧸ K₂) p) :
121	    K₁ = K₂ := by
122	  have hcomap : K₁ ≤ K₂.comap LinearMap.id := hle
123	  have hsurj : Function.Surjective (Submodule.mapQ K₁ K₂ LinearMap.id hcomap) := by
124	    intro y
125	    obtain ⟨x, rfl⟩ := Submodule.mkQ_surjective K₂ y
126	    exact ⟨Submodule.Quotient.mk x, rfl⟩
127	  have hinj := LinearMap.injective_of_surjective_of_rankAtStalk_eq _ hsurj hrank
128	  refine le_antisymm hle fun x hx => ?_
129	  have h0 : Submodule.mapQ K₁ K₂ LinearMap.id hcomap (Submodule.Quotient.mk x) = 0 := by
130	    rw [Submodule.mapQ_apply, LinearMap.id_apply]
131	    exact (Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero K₂).mpr hx
132	  have hx0 : (Submodule.Quotient.mk x : M ⧸ K₁) = 0 := hinj (by rw [h0, map_zero])
133	  exact (Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero K₁).mp hx0
134	
135	end RankEngine

152	/-! ## The window form of the projection identity -/
153	
154	section WindowEq
155	
156	variable {a g : ℕ} {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}

159	/-- **The window form of the ε-projection identity** (`informal/spec-dd-r.md` §3
160	item 5, the equality half): a Grassmannian point `x` whose submodule is contained in
161	the window submodule `K_a(d)` *equals* it, given the Θ-twisted colength certificate
162	slots (surjective evaluation + finite projective of constant rank `g`, exactly the
163	`divisorWindowGr` inputs).  Both quotients are then finite projective of rank `g`, and
164	nested submodules with same-rank quotients coincide by the rank engine.
165	
166	`hfin` and `hproj` are consumed by typeclass synthesis as local instances (they carry
167	the `Module.Finite`/`Module.Projective` slots into `Module.Finite.equiv` /
168	`Module.Projective.of_equiv`); the `unusedVariables` linter does not see the `hfin`
169	synthesis and is disabled here for that false positive. -/
170	theorem divisorWindow_eq_of_le (A : DivisorAdaptation C R π d)
171	    (hH1 : Subsingleton (relTwistPair C k π (relThetaCocycle C k π a)).H1)
172	    (x : Grassmannian.grFunctorAff k
173	      (↥(Scheme.divisorSections k (a • fiberWeilDivisor π) ⊤)) g R)
174	    (hsurj : Function.Surjective (A.thetaGluedEval a))
175	    (hfin : Module.Finite R (A.ThetaGlued a))
176	    (hproj : Module.Projective R (A.ThetaGlued a))
177	    (hrank : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R, Module.rankAtStalk (A.ThetaGlued a) p = g)
178	    (hle : x.toSubmodule ≤ divisorWindow d hH1) :
179	    divisorWindow d hH1 = x.toSubmodule := by
180	  haveI hfinW : Module.Finite R
181	      ((R ⊗[k] ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k (a • fiberWeilDivisor π) ⊤)) ⧸
182	        divisorWindow d hH1) :=
183	    Module.Finite.equiv (windowQuotEquiv A hH1 hsurj).symm
184	  haveI hprojW : Module.Projective R
185	      ((R ⊗[k] ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k (a • fiberWeilDivisor π) ⊤)) ⧸
186	        divisorWindow d hH1) :=
187	    Module.Projective.of_equiv (windowQuotEquiv A hH1 hsurj).symm
188	  refine (Submodule.eq_of_le_of_rankAtStalk_quotient_eq hle fun p => ?_).symm
189	  rw [x.rankAtStalk_eq p,
190	    congrFun (Module.rankAtStalk_eq_of_equiv (windowQuotEquiv A hH1 hsurj)) p,
191	    hrank p]
192	
193	/-- The window form of the ε-projection identity, with the colength certificate slots
194	discharged from the DD-1 certificate (`IsCertified.finite/projective/rankAtStalk_thetaGlued`,
195	the I-0211 keystones): only the surjectivity of the evaluation remains threaded. -/
196	theorem divisorWindow_eq_of_le_of_isCertified (A : DivisorAdaptation C R π d)
197	    (hc : A.IsCertified g)
198	    (hH1 : Subsingleton (relTwistPair C k π (relThetaCocycle C k π a)).H1)
199	    (x : Grassmannian.grFunctorAff k
200	      (↥(Scheme.divisorSections k (a • fiberWeilDivisor π) ⊤)) g R)
201	    (hsurj : Function.Surjective (A.thetaGluedEval a))
202	    (hle : x.toSubmodule ≤ divisorWindow d hH1) :
203	    divisorWindow d hH1 = x.toSubmodule :=
204	  divisorWindow_eq_of_le A hH1 x hsurj (hc.finite_thetaGlued a)
205	    (hc.projective_thetaGlued a) (fun p => hc.rankAtStalk_thetaGlued a p) hle

216	item 5): for a theta generator seed drawn from the Grassmannian point `x` — its
217	submodule `K` is the image of `x` under the window identification, the W1 spelling —
218	the window submodule of the constructed family is exactly `x`.  Containment is DDR-3's
219	`le_vanishingSubmodule` (the landed half); equality is the rank engine on the
220	certificate slots. -/
221	theorem ThetaGeneratorSeed.divisorWindow_eq
222	    (hH1 : Subsingleton (relTwistPair C k π (relThetaCocycle C k π a)).H1)
223	    (x : Grassmannian.grFunctorAff k
224	      (↥(Scheme.divisorSections k (a • fiberWeilDivisor π) ⊤)) g R)
225	    (D : ThetaGeneratorSeed C R π a
226	      (Submodule.map (relThetaWindowEquiv C R π a hH1).toLinearMap x.toSubmodule))
227	    (hD : D.IsGenerator) (hc : (D.divisorAdaptation hD).IsCertified g)
228	    (hsurj : Function.Surjective ((D.divisorAdaptation hD).thetaGluedEval a)) :
229	    divisorWindow (D.localEquations hD) hH1 = x.toSubmodule :=
230	  divisorWindow_eq_of_le_of_isCertified (D.divisorAdaptation hD) hc hH1 x hsurj
231	    (Submodule.map_le_iff_le_comap.mp (D.le_vanishingSubmodule hD))
232

235	local-equation system with its adaptation, bundled with a degree-`g` certificate (the
236	DDR-4 output) into the DD-1 carrier. -/

238	    {K : Submodule R (relThetaSections C R π a)} (D : ThetaGeneratorSeed C R π a K)

241	  eqns := D.localEquations hD
242	  adaptation := D.divisorAdaptation hD
243	  certified := hc

277	item 5): if the two window submodules of a certified family contain the Grassmannian
278	pair `(x₁, x₂)` at the pinned ledger exponents `M`, `M + s`, then `ε` of the family
279	*is* the pair.  The certificate slots fire from the family's own certificate
280	(I-0211); only the two evaluation surjectivities are threaded (the DD-4 Task-4
281	boundary, discharged by `thetaGluedEval_surjective` under `hfib`). -/
282	theorem divFamEps_mk_eq_of_le (G : CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π g)
283	    (x₁ : Grassmannian.grFunctorAff k
284	      (↥(Scheme.divisorSections k (windowM_choice π hπ g • fiberWeilDivisor π) ⊤)) g R)
285	    (x₂ : Grassmannian.grFunctorAff k
286	      (↥(Scheme.divisorSections k
287	        ((windowM_choice π hπ g + windowS_choice π hπ g) • fiberWeilDivisor π) ⊤)) g R)
288	    (hsurj₁ : Function.Surjective
289	      (G.adaptation.thetaGluedEval (windowM_choice π hπ g)))
290	    (hsurj₂ : Function.Surjective
291	      (G.adaptation.thetaGluedEval (windowM_choice π hπ g + windowS_choice π hπ g)))
292	    (hle₁ : x₁.toSubmodule ≤ divisorWindow G.eqns (relThetaPairH1_windowM C π hπ g))
293	    (hle₂ : x₂.toSubmodule ≤ divisorWindow G.eqns (relThetaPairH1_windowMS C π hπ g)) :
294	    divFamEps hπ g (DivFam.mk G) = (x₁.toSubmodule, x₂.toSubmodule) := by
295	  rw [divFamEps_mk]
296	  exact Prod.ext
297	    (divisorWindow_eq_of_le_of_isCertified G.adaptation G.certified
298	      (relThetaPairH1_windowM C π hπ g) x₁ hsurj₁ hle₁)
299	    (divisorWindow_eq_of_le_of_isCertified G.adaptation G.certified
300	      (relThetaPairH1_windowMS C π hπ g) x₂ hsurj₂ hle₂)

305	family constructed from a theta generator seed drawn from the Grassmannian point `x₁`
306	at the embedding window `M` is the tautological pair `(x₁, x₂)`.  The first-window
307	containment is DDR-3's `le_vanishingSubmodule`; the second-window containment `hle₂`
308	is the named DDR-5 boundary (fibrewise second-window exactness upgraded to relative
309	divisibility — the W2/DDR-4 fan-in; a fibrewise statement does NOT suffice over
310	nonreduced chart rings, spec risk 5).  The universal carve-pair instantiation is the
311	in-progress G-4 chain rooted at `AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivSchemeSeedUniv`. -/
312	theorem ThetaGeneratorSeed.divFamEps_certifiedFamily
313	    (x₁ : Grassmannian.grFunctorAff k
314	      (↥(Scheme.divisorSections k (windowM_choice π hπ g • fiberWeilDivisor π) ⊤)) g R)
315	    (x₂ : Grassmannian.grFunctorAff k
316	      (↥(Scheme.divisorSections k
317	        ((windowM_choice π hπ g + windowS_choice π hπ g) • fiberWeilDivisor π) ⊤)) g R)
318	    (D : ThetaGeneratorSeed C R π (windowM_choice π hπ g)
319	      (Submodule.map
320	        (relThetaWindowEquiv C R π (windowM_choice π hπ g)
321	          (relThetaPairH1_windowM C π hπ g)).toLinearMap x₁.toSubmodule))
322	    (hD : D.IsGenerator) (hc : (D.divisorAdaptation hD).IsCertified g)
323	    (hsurj₁ : Function.Surjective
324	      ((D.divisorAdaptation hD).thetaGluedEval (windowM_choice π hπ g)))
325	    (hsurj₂ : Function.Surjective
326	      ((D.divisorAdaptation hD).thetaGluedEval
327	        (windowM_choice π hπ g + windowS_choice π hπ g)))
328	    (hle₂ : x₂.toSubmodule ≤
329	      divisorWindow (D.localEquations hD) (relThetaPairH1_windowMS C π hπ g)) :
330	    divFamEps hπ g (DivFam.mk (D.certifiedFamily g hD hc))
331	      = (x₁.toSubmodule, x₂.toSubmodule) :=
332	  divFamEps_mk_eq_of_le hπ (D.certifiedFamily g hD hc) x₁ x₂ hsurj₁ hsurj₂

Base directory for this skill: /home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.claude/skills/blueprint-conventions

Blueprints are a LaTeX subset (the `leanblueprint` dialect) parsed into the DAG.
Write timeless mathematics — a standalone document, not a project journal.

## Environments

Each declaration is an amsthm-style environment; the recognized ones are
`theorem`, `lemma`, `proposition`, `corollary`, `definition`, `remark`,
`example`, `notation`, `convention`, and `proof`. A statement environment plus
its following `proof` environment form one node's content.

## Per-node macros

- `\label{id}` — a stable id (the DAG node key).
- `\lean{Name}` — the Lean declaration(s) this node formalizes; comma-separate to
  bind several (`\lean{a, b}`) when they jointly formalize the node's statement.
  Each named declaration's signature must match the statement. The mapping need
  not be 1-to-1: a node may name several declarations, and Lean may carry
  auxiliary declarations with no node at all.
- `\uses{a,b}` — dependencies on other nodes' labels; these drive the DAG edges.
  Add an edge instead of re-explaining a dependency in prose. Put `\uses` in the
  statement for definitional deps and in the `proof` for deps used only in the
  proof.
- `\source{slug:page-0001}` — reference anchors for UI popups and audit trails.
  Use page-level ids from `references/<slug>/tex/page-0001.tex` or an equivalent
  manifest entry. Multiple anchors may be comma-separated.
- `\leanok` — the Lean is written and checked. Honest only when its Lean is
  actually checked *and* its dependencies are too. On a `proof`, it means the
  proof is formalized; on a statement, the signature is formalized.
- `\mathlibok` — the declaration is already available in mathlib (no
  formalization needed; treat as a leaf).

## House style

- **Pure mathematics only.** No Lean tactics, typeclass/implementation notes, or
  semi-Lean pseudocode. No project history ("since iter N", "our failed route")
  and no conversational filler. Not every Lean helper needs its own node —
  auxiliary or implementation-only declarations can stay unnoded; add a node when
  the result is mathematically meaningful in its own right. In particular, never
  add a `Formalization note` paragraph to blueprint `.tex`: attach implementation
  details, failed approaches, and mechanization caveats to the statement's hgraph
  node with `horizon graph ... add comment` instead.
- **Complete proofs, not sketches.** A node's `proof` is a real, rigorous
  mathematical proof a reader could check — not a hand-wave or a TODO. The way to
  keep it short is to *split*, not to abbreviate: if a proof is long or a node
  grows past a short paragraph, break out the hard step as its own `\uses`-linked
  lemma (down to sentence-sized lemmas if needed) so each node stays small and
  its proof stays complete.
- **One statement's worth per node.** Keep each node to a single mathematical
  statement; don't restate Lean source as prose.
- **Cite by source link, not quote comments.** Add `\source{...}` to the
  relevant node. Keep the retrieved/transcribed page text in `references/` (for
  example `references/<slug>/tex/page-0042.tex`) and let the UI expose it; do not
  paste verbatim source quotes into `% QUOTE` comments inside the blueprint.

12	
13	This file isolates the formal tail between a chart-wise universal certified family and
14	the affine equivalence of DDR-9.F6.  It deliberately makes the remaining F5 hypotheses
15	explicit:
16	
17	* `divRepPullAt` pulls a supplied chart family along a map out of a carve-chart ring;
18	* `DivRepChartFamily.IsCompatible` is the exact choice-independence statement needed to
19	  glue those local pullbacks;
20	* `DivRepAffinePullback` packages the output of that glue together with the two laws and
21	  naturality;
22	* `DivRepAffinePullback.equiv` turns those data into the affine equivalence, using the
23	  already-landed uniqueness theorem for `divRepClassifyZar` for the hom-side law.
24	
25	No universal family, compatibility, inverse law, or representability theorem is asserted
26	here.  The future F5 construction must supply the fields of these interfaces.
27	-/

29	set_option autoImplicit false

42	section Curve
43	
44	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))}

10	/-!
11	# The big-site Zariski sheaf `pic⁰` and the 01JJ seam (DAT-6, stage 3)
12	
13	The slice trick assembled: the Σ-extension of the degree-zero Picard functor is an
14	honest sheaf for the big Zariski topology on `Scheme`, and mathlib's 01JJ
15	local-representability engine applied to it descends to a representation of the
16	degree-zero Picard functor itself on the slice.
17	
18	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0TypeFunctor C`: the degree-zero Picard functor with values in
19	  types — the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` massage of `pic0Functor`, owned here once
20	  (`pic0TypeFunctor_obj`/`pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply` are `rfl`).
21	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0SigmaFunctor C : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u`: the Σ-extension
22	  `T ↦ Σ (a : T ⟶ Spec k), pic⁰(Over.mk a)` — the big-site carrier.
23	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf` / **`pic0SigmaSheaf C`**: the sheaf
24	  certificate.  By mathlib's own reduction the big-site sheaf condition collapses to
25	  elementwise ∃!-amalgamation on honest open covers
26	  (`Precoverage.isSheaf_toGrothendieck_iff_of_isStableUnderBaseChange`,
27	  `exists_cover_of_mem_pretopology`, `Presieve.isSheafFor_arrows_iff` — the
28	  `BigZariski` TODO is never touched): the Σ-components glue by
29	  `Scheme.Cover.glueMorphisms`, the fibre components glue by the DAT-6 stage-1
30	  evaluation bridge (`pic0Subgroup_existsUnique_of_cover`), and the two layers are
31	  stitched by the stage-2 amalgamation seam (`sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff`) and
32	  compatibility descent (`map_eq_of_sigmaExtension_map_eq`).
33	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`: **the DAT-glue seam** — given a
34	  chart family of relatively representable open immersions into `pic0SigmaSheaf`
35	  (DAT-C) that is jointly locally surjective (DAT-B), mathlib's
36	  `Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy` produces a representation of the
37	  Σ-extension by the glued scheme, and the stage-2 Σ-descent `overSlice` turns it
38	  into a representation of `pic0TypeFunctor C` by the glued scheme over the
39	  Σ-component of the universal element.
40	-/
41

49

54	/-! ## The type-valued degree-zero Picard functor -/
55	
56	/-- The degree-zero Picard functor with values in types: the `forget₂ ⋙ forget`
57	massage of `pic0Functor`, owned here once for the Σ-extension statements. -/
58	noncomputable abbrev pic0TypeFunctor : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u :=
59	  (pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) ⋙ forget GrpCat
60	
61	@[simp]
62	lemma pic0TypeFunctor_obj (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) :
63	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).obj T = pic0Subgroup C T.unop :=
64	  rfl

66	lemma pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ} (g : T ⟶ T')
67	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C T.unop) :
68	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).map g lam = pic0Map C g.unop lam :=
69	  rfl

71	/-! ## The Σ-extension as a presheaf on the big site -/
72	
73	/-- **The big-site carrier of the slice trick**: the Σ-extension of the type-valued
74	degree-zero Picard functor, `T ↦ Σ (a : T ⟶ Spec k), pic⁰(Over.mk a)`.  Reducible so
75	that the stage-2 `sigmaExtension` calculus applies syntactically. -/
76	noncomputable abbrev pic0SigmaFunctor : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u :=
77	  Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (pic0TypeFunctor C)
78	
79	variable [GeometricallyReduced C.hom]
80	
81	set_option maxHeartbeats 800000 in
82	-- The amalgamation seams unify the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` massage of `pic0Functor`
83	-- against the Σ-extension calculus by unfolding; within the DAT-2/PicEtMap 1600000
84	-- precedent.
85	/-- **The big-site Zariski sheaf certificate of the Σ-extension** (DAT-6 keystone,
86	worksheet §1.2 site gap 1): mathlib's reduction collapses the sheaf condition to
87	elementwise ∃!-amalgamation on honest open covers, where the Σ-components glue by
88	`Scheme.Cover.glueMorphisms` and the fibre components by the stage-1 evaluation
89	bridge. -/
90	theorem pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf :
91	    Presieve.IsSheaf Scheme.zariskiTopology (pic0SigmaFunctor C) := by
92	  rw [Precoverage.isSheaf_toGrothendieck_iff_of_isStableUnderBaseChange]
93	  intro Y S hS
94	  obtain ⟨𝓤, rfl⟩ := Scheme.exists_cover_of_mem_pretopology hS
95	  rw [Presieve.isSheafFor_arrows_iff]
96	  intro x hx
97	  -- glue the Σ-components along the scheme-level cover
98	  have hpair : ∀ i j, pullback.fst (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j) ≫ (x i).1
99	      = pullback.snd (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j) ≫ (x j).1 := fun i j =>
100	    congrArg Sigma.fst
101	      (hx i j (pullback (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j)) (pullback.fst _ _) (pullback.snd _ _)
102	        pullback.condition)
103	  obtain ⟨aY, ha⟩ : ∃ aY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k), ∀ i, 𝓤.f i ≫ aY = (x i).1 :=
104	    ⟨𝓤.glueMorphisms (fun i => (x i).1) hpair,
105	      fun i => 𝓤.ι_glueMorphisms (fun i => (x i).1) hpair i⟩
106	  -- the induced slice cover of `Over.mk aY` and its member sections
107	  haveI hop : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion
108	      ((Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY)).left :=
109	    fun i => 𝓤.map_prop i
110	  have hcov : ∀ p : (Over.mk aY).left, ∃ i, p ∈ Scheme.Hom.opensRange
111	      ((Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY)).left := by
112	    intro p
113	    obtain ⟨i, y, hy⟩ := 𝓤.exists_eq p
114	    exact ⟨i, y, hy⟩
115	  -- the fibre components are a compatible family on the slice cover
116	  have hcompat : ∀ (i j : 𝓤.I₀) (Z : Over (Spec (.of k)))
117	      (gi : Z ⟶ Over.mk ((x i).1)) (gj : Z ⟶ Over.mk ((x j).1)),
118	      gi ≫ (Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY)
119	          = gj ≫ (Over.homMk (𝓤.f j) (ha j) : Over.mk ((x j).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY) →
120	      pic0Map C gi ((x i).2) = pic0Map C gj ((x j).2) := by
121	    intro i j Z gi gj hg
122	    have hleft : gi.left ≫ 𝓤.f i = gj.left ≫ 𝓤.f j := congrArg Over.Hom.left hg
123	    have hdesc := Over.map_eq_of_sigmaExtension_map_eq gi gj
124	      (hx i j Z.left gi.left gj.left hleft)
125	    rwa [pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply, pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply] at hdesc
126	  -- glue the fibre components by the stage-1 evaluation bridge
127	  obtain ⟨s, hs, hsu⟩ := pic0Subgroup_existsUnique_of_cover
128	    (fun i => (Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY))
129	    hcov (fun i => (x i).2) hcompat
130	  refine ⟨⟨aY, s⟩, fun i => ?_, ?_⟩
131	  · -- the glued Σ-element restricts to the members
132	    refine (Over.sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff (𝓤.f i) (ha i) s ((x i).2)).mpr ?_
133	    rw [pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply]
134	    exact hs i
135	  · -- uniqueness: Σ-components by `hom_ext`, fibres by bridge separation
136	    rintro ⟨a', s'⟩ ht'
137	    obtain rfl : aY = a' := 𝓤.hom_ext aY a' fun i =>
138	      (ha i).trans (congrArg Sigma.fst (ht' i) : 𝓤.f i ≫ a' = (x i).1).symm
139	    refine congrArg (Sigma.mk aY) (hsu s' fun i => ?_)
140	    have hmem := (Over.sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff (𝓤.f i) (ha i) s' ((x i).2)).mp
141	      (ht' i)
142	    rwa [pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply] at hmem
143	
144	/-- **The Σ-extension of the degree-zero Picard functor, bundled as a sheaf on the
145	big Zariski site** — the object mathlib's 01JJ local-representability engine
146	consumes. -/
147	noncomputable def pic0SigmaSheaf : Sheaf Scheme.zariskiTopology.{u} (Type u) :=
148	  ⟨pic0SigmaFunctor C,
149	    (isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_of_type _ _).mpr (pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf C)⟩
150	
151	/-! ## The DAT-glue seam -/
152	
153	/-- **The DAT-glue statement (worksheet §4, DAT-glue row)**: a chart family of
154	relatively representable open immersions into the Σ-extension sheaf (DAT-C's
155	certificates) that is jointly Zariski-locally surjective (DAT-B's coverage) induces —
156	through mathlib's 01JJ engine and the stage-2 Σ-descent — a representation of the
157	type-valued degree-zero Picard functor by the glued scheme placed over the
158	Σ-component of the universal element.  The represented object's `.left` is
159	`(Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued` and its `.hom` is the universal
160	element's Σ-component, both definitionally. -/
161	noncomputable def pic0RepresentableByOfCharts
162	    {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
163	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
164	    (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i))
165	    [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)] :
166	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy
167	      (Over.mk ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv
168	        (𝟙 (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued)).1) :=
169	  (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).overSlice
170

8	/-!
9	# The Jacobian representability datum (Wave-4 seam D1, `JacobianData`)
10	
11	The pinned representability datum for the degree-zero étale-sheafified relative Picard
12	functor `pic0Functor C` of the challenge curve: a representing object `J`, an honest
13	`Functor.RepresentableBy` datum (no `Nonempty`, no choice), and the two construction
14	certificates (`LocallyOfFiniteType`, `QuasiCompact`).  This is the frozen Wave-4
15	interface shape (`informal/w4-datum-worksheet.md` §1.1, verbatim), together with the
16	design-§5 consumers `grpObj` / `homEquiv` / `uniqueUpToIso` — and nothing else.
17	
18	## Ownership split (binding, w5-worksheet D1)
19	
20	* The **producer** `jacobianData C : JacobianData C`, the quasi-compactness certificate,
21	  and the discharge of the frozen `Jacobian`/`instGrpObj` sorries of `Challenge.lean`
22	  are **DAT-J property** (the parallel Wave-4 fleet).  None of them lives here.
23	* This file is the **Wave-5/6/7 consumption interface**: downstream files take
24	  `(d : JacobianData C)` as a section variable, activate the group structure per proof
25	  via `letI := d.grpObj` (or `attribute [local instance] JacobianData.grpObj`), and
26	  phrase every statement about `d.J`.  At DAT-J discharge time the frozen gate
27	  instantiates them by `exact theorem_x … (jacobianData C)` — definitionally, since
28	  `Jacobian C := (jacobianData C).J`.
29	* Extensions to this file are **additive only**; the structure shape never changes.
30	
31	## The `forget₂ ⋙ forget` massage
32	
33	`rep` is typed against `(pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) ⋙ forget GrpCat`
34	so that mathlib's `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` applies **verbatim** with
35	`F := pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat`.  The functor value at a test `T` is
36	*definitionally* the coerced subgroup `↥(pic0Subgroup C T)`; `homEquiv` and
37	`homEquiv_comp` below own this defeq once, exposing the equivalence against
38	`pic0Subgroup C T` and the naturality against `pic0Map` — no consumer ever meets the
39	`forget₂ ⋙ forget` spelling again.
40	
41	## η-defeq verdict (recon §5 "lower-order unknown", RECORDED)
42	
43	**POSITIVE, with one keying caveat.**  `Over.mk d.J.hom` is definitionally equal to
44	`d.J` (structure-eta for `Comma`/`CostructuredArrow` plus unit-like eta for the
45	`Discrete PUnit` right leg): the ascription
46	`(d.grpObj : GrpObj (Over.mk d.J.hom))` elaborates as-is, so **no transport lemma is
47	ever needed**.  Caveat: bare instance *search* does not unfold `Over.mk` on its own,
48	so a consumer of `smooth_of_grpObj` — whose group hypothesis is `[GrpObj (Over.mk f)]`
49	at `f := d.J.hom` — must key the instance at the `Over.mk` spelling:
50	`letI : GrpObj (Over.mk d.J.hom) := d.grpObj` (pure defeq, zero cost; mathlib itself
51	uses the same ascription idiom in `Group/Smooth.lean`).  Instances stated directly on
52	`G : Over (Spec (.of K))` (e.g. `IsClosedImmersion η[G].left`) fire on `d.J` with no
53	massage at all.  The `example`-level smoke tests at the bottom of this file are the
54	machine-checked record; the T-chain (tangent lane) and S2 (`Smooth` via
55	`smooth_of_grpObj`) may rely on this freely.
56	
57	## Main declarations
58	
59	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData C` — the frozen datum structure.
60	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.grpObj` — the group-object structure on `d.J` via
61	  `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` (the discharge route of the frozen `instGrpObj`).
62	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.homEquiv` / `homEquiv_comp` — the universal property
63	  in consumer form: `(T ⟶ d.J) ≃ pic0Subgroup C T`, natural against `pic0Map`.
64	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.uniqueUpToIso` / `homEquiv_uniqueUpToIso_hom` — any
65	  two data have canonically isomorphic representing objects (Wave-7's `baseChangeIso`
66	  mechanism), with the intertwining property.
67	-/

78	variable {k : Type u} [Field k]

80	/-- **The pinned representability datum** for the degree-zero étale-sheafified relative
81	Picard functor of the curve `C` (w4-datum-worksheet §1.1, frozen).  Produced once, by
82	explicit construction, in Wave 4 (DAT-J: `jacobianData`); consumed as a section
83	variable everywhere else.  NEVER a sorried instance, NEVER `Nonempty` + choice.
84	
85	The typing of `rep` is chosen so that `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` applies verbatim with
86	`F := pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat` (see `JacobianData.grpObj`). -/
87	structure JacobianData (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
88	    [IsProper C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
89	    Type (u + 1) where
90	  /-- The representing object (the Jacobian-to-be). -/
91	  J : Over (Spec (.of k))
92	  /-- The pinned universal datum: `Hom(T, J) ≃ Pic⁰(T)`, naturally in the test `T`. -/
93	  rep : ((pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) ⋙ forget GrpCat).RepresentableBy J
94	  /-- Certificate from the construction (Kleiman 4.8(1) shape); NOT re-derived via the
95	  EGA limit criterion. -/
96	  locallyOfFiniteType : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom
97	  /-- Certificate from the construction (a posteriori: `|J|` is the image of a
98	  quasi-compact divisor scheme under the Abel map).  Feeds `IsProper` (Wave 5) via
99	  `finite type = qc + lft`. -/
100	  quasiCompact : QuasiCompact J.hom
101	
102	namespace JacobianData
103	
104	variable {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
105	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
106	
107	/-- The group-object structure on the representing object, via mathlib's
108	`GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` — this is the (definitional) discharge route of the frozen
109	`Jacobian.instGrpObj`.  Not a global instance here (the datum is a section variable);
110	activate per proof with `letI := d.grpObj` or
111	`attribute [local instance] JacobianData.grpObj`. -/
112	@[implicit_reducible]
113	noncomputable def grpObj (d : JacobianData C) : GrpObj d.J :=
114	  GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy d.J (pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) d.rep
115	
116	/-- **The universal property, consumer form**: morphisms into `d.J` are degree-zero
117	étale Picard classes.  This accessor owns the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` defeq massage once:
118	the target is the honest subgroup carrier `pic0Subgroup C T`. -/
119	def homEquiv (d : JacobianData C) {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} :
120	    (T ⟶ d.J) ≃ pic0Subgroup C T :=
121	  d.rep.homEquiv
122	
123	/-- Naturality of `homEquiv` against the degree-zero restriction maps `pic0Map`
124	(element form of the `RepresentableBy` naturality, with the functor value unfolded
125	through `forget₂ ⋙ forget`). -/
126	theorem homEquiv_comp (d : JacobianData C) {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))}
127	    (f : T' ⟶ T) (g : T ⟶ d.J) :
128	    d.homEquiv (f ≫ g) = pic0Map C f (d.homEquiv g) :=
129	  d.rep.homEquiv_comp f g
130	
131	/-- Representing objects are unique up to isomorphism (mathlib
132	`Functor.RepresentableBy.uniqueUpToIso`): any two Jacobian data for the same curve have
133	canonically isomorphic `J`.  This is Wave-7's `baseChangeIso` mechanism. -/
134	noncomputable def uniqueUpToIso (d d' : JacobianData C) : d.J ≅ d'.J :=
135	  d.rep.uniqueUpToIso d'.rep
136	
137	/-- The intertwining property of `uniqueUpToIso`: composing with the canonical
138	isomorphism commutes with the two universal properties. -/
139	theorem homEquiv_uniqueUpToIso_hom (d d' : JacobianData C) {T : Over (Spec (.of k))}
140	    (f : T ⟶ d.J) :
141	    d'.homEquiv (f ≫ (d.uniqueUpToIso d').hom) = d.homEquiv f := by
142	  have h : (d.uniqueUpToIso d').hom = d'.rep.homEquiv.symm (d.rep.homEquiv (𝟙 d.J)) := rfl
143	  rw [homEquiv, homEquiv, h, Functor.RepresentableBy.comp_homEquiv_symm]
144	  exact (d'.rep.homEquiv.apply_symm_apply _).trans (d.rep.homEquiv_eq f).symm
145	
146	end JacobianData
147	
148	/-! ## η-defeq smoke tests (recon §5 lower-order unknown; `example`-level, nothing
149	registered)
150	
151	The first test records that `Over.mk d.J.hom ≡ d.J` definitionally (structure eta); the
152	second that instance resolution crosses it — `smooth_of_grpObj`'s hypothesis
153	`[GrpObj (Over.mk f)]` at `f := d.J.hom` is discharged by `letI := d.grpObj`; the third
154	that mathlib's `IsClosedImmersion η[d.J].left` instance fires on `d.J` as-is.  T-chain
155	and S2 depend on these; if a mathlib bump ever breaks them, a transport lemma must be
156	added HERE, not in the consumers. -/
157	
158	section EtaDefeqSmokeTests
159	
160	open MonObj
161	
162	variable {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
163	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
164	
165	/-- Smoke test 1: `Over.mk d.J.hom` is definitionally `d.J` — the ascription
166	elaborates with no transport. -/
167	noncomputable example (d : JacobianData C) : GrpObj (Over.mk d.J.hom) := d.grpObj
168	
169	/-- Smoke test 2: `smooth_of_grpObj` applies to `d.J.hom` with no transport lemma;
170	the group instance must be *keyed* at `Over.mk d.J.hom` (the ascribed `letI` below —
171	instance search does not unfold `Over.mk` on its own, but the ascription is pure
172	defeq). -/
173	example (d : JacobianData C) [GeometricallyReduced d.J.hom] : Smooth d.J.hom :=
174	  letI := d.locallyOfFiniteType
175	  letI : GrpObj (Over.mk d.J.hom) := d.grpObj
176	  smooth_of_grpObj d.J.hom
177	
178	/-- Smoke test 3: the unit section of `d.J` is a closed immersion (mathlib's
179	group-scheme instance fires on `d.J` directly, with the datum's group structure in
180	scope). -/
181	example (d : JacobianData C) [GrpObj d.J] : IsClosedImmersion η[d.J].left :=
182	  inferInstance
183	
184	end EtaDefeqSmokeTests
185	
186	end AlgebraicGeometry

1	/-

4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
5	-/
6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEtCoverBridge
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.OverSigmaExtension
8	import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Sites.Representability
9	
10	/-!
11	# The big-site Zariski sheaf `pic⁰` and the 01JJ seam (DAT-6, stage 3)
12	
13	The slice trick assembled: the Σ-extension of the degree-zero Picard functor is an
14	honest sheaf for the big Zariski topology on `Scheme`, and mathlib's 01JJ
15	local-representability engine applied to it descends to a representation of the
16	degree-zero Picard functor itself on the slice.
17	
18	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0TypeFunctor C`: the degree-zero Picard functor with values in
19	  types — the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` massage of `pic0Functor`, owned here once
20	  (`pic0TypeFunctor_obj`/`pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply` are `rfl`).
21	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0SigmaFunctor C : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u`: the Σ-extension
22	  `T ↦ Σ (a : T ⟶ Spec k), pic⁰(Over.mk a)` — the big-site carrier.
23	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf` / **`pic0SigmaSheaf C`**: the sheaf
24	  certificate.  By mathlib's own reduction the big-site sheaf condition collapses to
25	  elementwise ∃!-amalgamation on honest open covers
26	  (`Precoverage.isSheaf_toGrothendieck_iff_of_isStableUnderBaseChange`,
27	  `exists_cover_of_mem_pretopology`, `Presieve.isSheafFor_arrows_iff` — the
28	  `BigZariski` TODO is never touched): the Σ-components glue by
29	  `Scheme.Cover.glueMorphisms`, the fibre components glue by the DAT-6 stage-1
30	  evaluation bridge (`pic0Subgroup_existsUnique_of_cover`), and the two layers are
31	  stitched by the stage-2 amalgamation seam (`sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff`) and
32	  compatibility descent (`map_eq_of_sigmaExtension_map_eq`).
33	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`: **the DAT-glue seam** — given a
34	  chart family of relatively representable open immersions into `pic0SigmaSheaf`
35	  (DAT-C) that is jointly locally surjective (DAT-B), mathlib's
36	  `Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy` produces a representation of the
37	  Σ-extension by the glued scheme, and the stage-2 Σ-descent `overSlice` turns it
38	  into a representation of `pic0TypeFunctor C` by the glued scheme over the
39	  Σ-component of the universal element.
40	-/
41	
42	set_option autoImplicit false
43	
44	universe u
45	
46	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite
47	
48	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
49	
50	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
51	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
52	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
53	
54	/-! ## The type-valued degree-zero Picard functor -/
55	
56	/-- The degree-zero Picard functor with values in types: the `forget₂ ⋙ forget`
57	massage of `pic0Functor`, owned here once for the Σ-extension statements. -/
58	noncomputable abbrev pic0TypeFunctor : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u :=
59	  (pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) ⋙ forget GrpCat
60	
61	@[simp]
62	lemma pic0TypeFunctor_obj (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) :
63	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).obj T = pic0Subgroup C T.unop :=
64	  rfl
65	
66	lemma pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ} (g : T ⟶ T')
67	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C T.unop) :
68	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).map g lam = pic0Map C g.unop lam :=
69	  rfl
70	
71	/-! ## The Σ-extension as a presheaf on the big site -/
72	
73	/-- **The big-site carrier of the slice trick**: the Σ-extension of the type-valued
74	degree-zero Picard functor, `T ↦ Σ (a : T ⟶ Spec k), pic⁰(Over.mk a)`.  Reducible so
75	that the stage-2 `sigmaExtension` calculus applies syntactically. -/
76	noncomputable abbrev pic0SigmaFunctor : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u :=
77	  Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (pic0TypeFunctor C)
78	
79	variable [GeometricallyReduced C.hom]
80	
81	set_option maxHeartbeats 800000 in
82	-- The amalgamation seams unify the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` massage of `pic0Functor`
83	-- against the Σ-extension calculus by unfolding; within the DAT-2/PicEtMap 1600000
84	-- precedent.
85	/-- **The big-site Zariski sheaf certificate of the Σ-extension** (DAT-6 keystone,
86	worksheet §1.2 site gap 1): mathlib's reduction collapses the sheaf condition to
87	elementwise ∃!-amalgamation on honest open covers, where the Σ-components glue by
88	`Scheme.Cover.glueMorphisms` and the fibre components by the stage-1 evaluation
89	bridge. -/
90	theorem pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf :
91	    Presieve.IsSheaf Scheme.zariskiTopology (pic0SigmaFunctor C) := by
92	  rw [Precoverage.isSheaf_toGrothendieck_iff_of_isStableUnderBaseChange]
93	  intro Y S hS
94	  obtain ⟨𝓤, rfl⟩ := Scheme.exists_cover_of_mem_pretopology hS
95	  rw [Presieve.isSheafFor_arrows_iff]
96	  intro x hx
97	  -- glue the Σ-components along the scheme-level cover
98	  have hpair : ∀ i j, pullback.fst (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j) ≫ (x i).1
99	      = pullback.snd (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j) ≫ (x j).1 := fun i j =>
100	    congrArg Sigma.fst
101	      (hx i j (pullback (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j)) (pullback.fst _ _) (pullback.snd _ _)
102	        pullback.condition)
103	  obtain ⟨aY, ha⟩ : ∃ aY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k), ∀ i, 𝓤.f i ≫ aY = (x i).1 :=
104	    ⟨𝓤.glueMorphisms (fun i => (x i).1) hpair,
105	      fun i => 𝓤.ι_glueMorphisms (fun i => (x i).1) hpair i⟩
106	  -- the induced slice cover of `Over.mk aY` and its member sections
107	  haveI hop : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion
108	      ((Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY)).left :=
109	    fun i => 𝓤.map_prop i
110	  have hcov : ∀ p : (Over.mk aY).left, ∃ i, p ∈ Scheme.Hom.opensRange
111	      ((Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY)).left := by
112	    intro p
113	    obtain ⟨i, y, hy⟩ := 𝓤.exists_eq p
114	    exact ⟨i, y, hy⟩
115	  -- the fibre components are a compatible family on the slice cover
116	  have hcompat : ∀ (i j : 𝓤.I₀) (Z : Over (Spec (.of k)))
117	      (gi : Z ⟶ Over.mk ((x i).1)) (gj : Z ⟶ Over.mk ((x j).1)),
118	      gi ≫ (Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY)
119	          = gj ≫ (Over.homMk (𝓤.f j) (ha j) : Over.mk ((x j).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY) →
120	      pic0Map C gi ((x i).2) = pic0Map C gj ((x j).2) := by
121	    intro i j Z gi gj hg
122	    have hleft : gi.left ≫ 𝓤.f i = gj.left ≫ 𝓤.f j := congrArg Over.Hom.left hg
123	    have hdesc := Over.map_eq_of_sigmaExtension_map_eq gi gj
124	      (hx i j Z.left gi.left gj.left hleft)
125	    rwa [pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply, pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply] at hdesc
126	  -- glue the fibre components by the stage-1 evaluation bridge
127	  obtain ⟨s, hs, hsu⟩ := pic0Subgroup_existsUnique_of_cover
128	    (fun i => (Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY))
129	    hcov (fun i => (x i).2) hcompat
130	  refine ⟨⟨aY, s⟩, fun i => ?_, ?_⟩
131	  · -- the glued Σ-element restricts to the members
132	    refine (Over.sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff (𝓤.f i) (ha i) s ((x i).2)).mpr ?_
133	    rw [pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply]
134	    exact hs i
135	  · -- uniqueness: Σ-components by `hom_ext`, fibres by bridge separation
136	    rintro ⟨a', s'⟩ ht'
137	    obtain rfl : aY = a' := 𝓤.hom_ext aY a' fun i =>
138	      (ha i).trans (congrArg Sigma.fst (ht' i) : 𝓤.f i ≫ a' = (x i).1).symm
139	    refine congrArg (Sigma.mk aY) (hsu s' fun i => ?_)
140	    have hmem := (Over.sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff (𝓤.f i) (ha i) s' ((x i).2)).mp
141	      (ht' i)
142	    rwa [pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply] at hmem
143	
144	/-- **The Σ-extension of the degree-zero Picard functor, bundled as a sheaf on the
145	big Zariski site** — the object mathlib's 01JJ local-representability engine
146	consumes. -/
147	noncomputable def pic0SigmaSheaf : Sheaf Scheme.zariskiTopology.{u} (Type u) :=
148	  ⟨pic0SigmaFunctor C,
149	    (isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_of_type _ _).mpr (pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf C)⟩
150	
151	/-! ## The DAT-glue seam -/
152	
153	/-- **The DAT-glue statement (worksheet §4, DAT-glue row)**: a chart family of
154	relatively representable open immersions into the Σ-extension sheaf (DAT-C's
155	certificates) that is jointly Zariski-locally surjective (DAT-B's coverage) induces —
156	through mathlib's 01JJ engine and the stage-2 Σ-descent — a representation of the
157	type-valued degree-zero Picard functor by the glued scheme placed over the
158	Σ-component of the universal element.  The represented object's `.left` is
159	`(Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued` and its `.hom` is the universal
160	element's Σ-component, both definitionally. -/
161	noncomputable def pic0RepresentableByOfCharts
162	    {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
163	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
164	    (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i))
165	    [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)] :
166	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy
167	      (Over.mk ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv
168	        (𝟙 (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued)).1) :=
169	  (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).overSlice
170	
171	end AlgebraicGeometry

Base directory for this skill: /home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.claude/skills/references

`references/` is a **shared library at the workspace root** — one library for
every project — holding the original source material a blueprint is formalised
from (papers, books, notes). It is indexed by `references/manifest.yaml`. Per-
project files live under each project's directory; `references/` does not — it is
always at the workspace root, and `references/**` is writable from any agent.

A blueprint node derived from a source carries a `\source{...}` anchor. Those
anchors are the audit trail from a formal statement back to where it came from,
so they must be **true**, not plausible.

## The one rule: read before you cite

**Never add a `\source{...}` anchor to a source you have not actually read.** Do
not infer a citation from a title, a topic, a theorem number, or your own prior
knowledge of the result. An anchor asserts "this exact statement/proof appears
here" — if you haven't opened the referenced material and confirmed it, you don't
know that, and a wrong anchor is worse than none (it sends the next reader/agent
to the wrong place and launders a guess as provenance).

Concretely, before writing `\source{...}`:
1. Confirm the source exists in `references/manifest.yaml`. If it isn't there,
   get it in first (see below) — don't cite a slug that doesn't resolve.
2. Open the actual content — the TeX, or the transcribed page — and confirm the
   statement/proof you're anchoring is really there.
3. Only then write the anchor.

## Anchor forms — pick by what the source actually is

The manifest's `read` field for each entry tells you which case you're in.

- **The source has LaTeX** (arXiv e-print, an open `.tex`, etc.): read the TeX
  directly and cite the source as a whole — `\source{slug}`. Do **not** invent a
  `page-NNNN`; a TeX source has no rendered pages, so a page number would be
  fabricated. If the manifest documents stable sub-ids for the source (a section
  or label id), you may use `\source{slug:<id>}`, but only an id that exists.
- **The source is PDF-only** (no usable TeX): cite the transcribed page,
  `\source{slug:page-NNNN}`, where `page-NNNN` is a real file under
  `references/<slug>/tex/page-NNNN.tex` that you have read. If that page hasn't
  been transcribed yet, transcribe it first (below) — don't cite a page that
  doesn't exist on disk.

Multiple anchors may be comma-separated: `\source{slug:page-0042, other:page-0007}`.

## Getting a source into the library

Don't fetch and stash sources ad hoc. Spawn the **`reference-retriever`** subagent
(by name, through your engine's native subagent mechanism) with whatever you have
— topic, arXiv ID, DOI, title, URL, target page range. It downloads the original
(preferring TeX, keeping the PDF), verifies the file is real (not a paywall/login
page named `.pdf`), organises it under `references/<slug>/`, and registers it in
`references/manifest.yaml`. Wait for it, then cite from what it wrote.

## Extracting the LaTeX from a PDF-only source

When there is no reliable TeX and you need the actual math (to read it, or to cite
a page), **extract it with the proper tool — don't eyeball the PDF and paraphrase.**
The extraction path is the **`page-transcriber`** subagent, which renders each page
to an image and **vision-transcribes** it into one self-contained
`references/<slug>/tex/page-NNNN.tex` per page.

- **Vision, never OCR.** OCR mangles math (subscripts, operators, alignment);
  reading the rendered page image with a vision model preserves it. This is a hard
  rule of the transcription flow.
- **A small vision model is usually enough.** Faithful page transcription doesn't
  need a frontier model — a cheap vision-capable model typically suffices. The
  Horizon agent chooses the model and effort at dispatch time; do not encode that
  spend policy in `config.yaml` or the descriptor.
- **Keep each call ≤5 pages.** Longer ranges lose accuracy; split a big range
  across several `page-transcriber` calls.

## Reading transcriptions correctly

- A transcribed page is `references/<slug>/tex/page-NNNN.tex` where `NNNN` is the
  **PDF page index**, which often differs from the printed page number. The
  manifest entry's `read` field records the `page_offset` and any fallback that
  actually worked — respect it when mapping "Theorem 3.4 on p. 12" to a file.
- Read the whole page file before citing it; a page can hold several results.

## The manifest at a glance

One entry per source (the `reference-retriever` owns the full schema):

```yaml
references:
  - slug: <slug>
    title: <title>
    source: <arXiv ID / DOI / URL>
    status: ok            # or: not_found
    files:
      - { path: <slug>/<slug>.pdf, format: pdf }
      - { path: <slug>/source.tex, format: tex }        # if TeX obtained
      - { path: <slug>/tex/page-0042.tex, format: tex } # if transcribed
    read: "Read TeX when present; else page anchors slug:page-NNNN. page_offset: ..."
```

If a source can't be found and verified, it's recorded `status: not_found` — treat
that as "no citation available," and write no math attributed to it.

Related skills: `blueprint-conventions` for where `\source{...}` sits among the
other blueprint annotations, and `hgraph` for how a node's `sources` feed the DAG.

1	/-

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.GluedSheafDatum

8	import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.ChartColength
9	import Mathlib.RingTheory.Spectrum.Prime.FreeLocus

11	/-!
12	# Certified divisor families: the DD-1 carrier (`informal/spec-dd-1.md` §1)
13	
14	The Wave-4 DAT-D divisor functor's object data over an affine test `R`, the worksheet's
15	(D1) pin (`informal/dat-d-worksheet.md` §1.1): a `LocalEquations` system `d` on the
16	relative curve `C_R = relCurve C R`, a **finite chart adaptation** refining it — finitely
17	many basic opens `D(h_j)` of the two pinned charts with partition witnesses, carrying
18	regular equations `f_j` that agree with `d`'s equations up to units — and the **colength
19	certificate**: the chart-local colength modules `Γ(D(h_j))/(f_j)` are finite projective
20	over `R`, and the glued equalizer module `W(d)` is finite projective of constant fibre
21	rank `n` (`Module.rankAtStalk`), with the two flat-cokernel clauses (c3)/(c4) that make
22	certificates base-change (`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.FlatCokernel`).
23	
24	* `AlgebraicGeometry.FinCoverData` — the `Fin`-indexed basic-open cover data (`Type u`;
25	  DAT-1's `BasicOpenCoverData` shape is `Type (u+1)`, unusable inside a functor value).
26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation` — the adaptation: equations + the pointwise
27	  refinement-up-to-units clause `eqn_rel` (point-free, so it pulls back along arbitrary
28	  morphisms), with the anchored constructor `DivisorAdaptation.ofAnchors`.
29	* `DivisorAdaptation.gluedSubmodule` — the glued colength module
30	  `W(d) = ker (δ⁻ − δ⁺) ⊆ Π_j Γ(D(h_j))/(f_j)`, with the equalizer description
31	  `mem_gluedSubmodule_iff` (the worksheet's `eq(∏_j ⇉ ∏_{j,j'})`).
32	* `DivisorAdaptation.IsCertified` — the certificate (c1)–(c4).
33	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq` — divisor equality of local-equation
34	  systems: on a common refinement the equations agree up to units (refinement +
35	  rescaling in one move), an equivalence relation with
36	  `picClass_eq_of_divEq` (the class laws `picClass_restrict`/`picClass_rescale`).
37	* `AlgebraicGeometry.CertifiedDivisorFamily`, `AlgebraicGeometry.DivFam` — the certified
38	  family and the setoid quotient `DivFam C π n R : Type u`, the divisor functor's value
39	  on the affine test `R`, with `DivFam.picClass`.
40	
41	The `R`-algebra structure on section rings is `Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra` through
42	`relCurve.instOver` (LOCAL instances, house rule) — consumers must activate the same
43	instances.
44	-/

56	/-! ## Divisor equality of local-equation systems (the setoid relation)
57	
58	Generic in the scheme; this is pure `DivisorClass`-level material. -/
59	
60	namespace Scheme.LocalEquations
61	
62	variable {X : Scheme.{u}}
63	
64	/-- Restriction of a section along `W ≤ V ≤ U` composes to restriction along `W ≤ U`. -/
65	private lemma res_res {W V U : X.Opens} (h₁ : W ≤ V) (h₂ : V ≤ U) (s : Γ(X, U)) :
66	    (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE h₁).op).hom ((X.presheaf.map (homOfLE h₂).op).hom s)
67	      = (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (h₁.trans h₂)).op).hom s := by
68	  rw [← CommRingCat.comp_apply, ← Functor.map_comp, ← op_comp, homOfLE_comp]
69	
70	/-- **Divisor equality** of two local-equation systems: on a common refinement of the
71	two covers, the equations agree up to a unit at every point — common refinement plus
72	unit rescaling in a single move (the `CechPic`-pattern setoid of the DD-1 spec). -/
73	def DivEq (d₁ d₂ : X.LocalEquations) : Prop :=
74	  ∃ (𝒲 : X.PointedCover) (h₁ : 𝒲 ≤ d₁.cover) (h₂ : 𝒲 ≤ d₂.cover),
75	    ∀ x : X, ∃ u : Γ(X, 𝒲.opens x)ˣ,
76	      (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (h₁ x)).op).hom (d₁.eqn x)
77	        = (u : Γ(X, 𝒲.opens x))
78	          * (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (h₂ x)).op).hom (d₂.eqn x)
79	
80	lemma divEq_refl (d : X.LocalEquations) : DivEq d d :=
81	  ⟨d.cover, le_rfl, le_rfl, fun _ => ⟨1, by rw [Units.val_one, one_mul]⟩⟩
82	
83	lemma DivEq.symm {d₁ d₂ : X.LocalEquations} (h : DivEq d₁ d₂) : DivEq d₂ d₁ := by
84	  obtain ⟨𝒲, h₁, h₂, H⟩ := h
85	  refine ⟨𝒲, h₂, h₁, fun x => ?_⟩
86	  obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := H x
87	  exact ⟨u⁻¹, by
88	    rw [hu, ← mul_assoc, ← Units.val_mul, inv_mul_cancel, Units.val_one, one_mul]⟩
89	
90	lemma DivEq.trans {d₁ d₂ d₃ : X.LocalEquations} (h : DivEq d₁ d₂) (h' : DivEq d₂ d₃) :
91	    DivEq d₁ d₃ := by
92	  obtain ⟨𝒲, h₁, h₂, H⟩ := h
93	  obtain ⟨𝒱, k₂, k₃, K⟩ := h'
94	  refine ⟨𝒲 ⊓ 𝒱, fun x => (inf_le_left (b := 𝒱.opens x)).trans (h₁ x),
95	    fun x => (inf_le_right (a := 𝒲.opens x)).trans (k₃ x), fun x => ?_⟩
96	  obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := H x
97	  obtain ⟨v, hv⟩ := K x
98	  have E1 := congrArg (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE
99	    (inf_le_left : 𝒲.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒲.opens x)).op).hom hu
100	  rw [map_mul, res_res, res_res] at E1
101	  have E2 := congrArg (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE
102	    (inf_le_right : 𝒲.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒱.opens x)).op).hom hv
103	  rw [map_mul, res_res, res_res] at E2
104	  refine ⟨X.unitsRestrict inf_le_left u * X.unitsRestrict inf_le_right v, ?_⟩
105	  have hcast : ∀ (w : Γ(X, 𝒲.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x)ˣ), (w : Γ(X, 𝒲.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x))
106	      = w.val := fun _ => rfl
107	  rw [Units.val_mul]
108	  calc (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE _).op).hom (d₁.eqn x)
109	      = (X.unitsRestrict inf_le_left u).val
110	        * (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE ((inf_le_right).trans (k₂ x))).op).hom (d₂.eqn x) := by
111	        rw [show (X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_left :
112	            𝒲.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒲.opens x) u).val
113	            = (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left :
114	                𝒲.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒲.opens x)).op).hom u.val from rfl]
115	        exact E1
116	    _ = (X.unitsRestrict inf_le_left u).val * ((X.unitsRestrict inf_le_right v).val
117	        * (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE ((inf_le_right).trans (k₃ x))).op).hom (d₃.eqn x)) := by
118	        rw [show (X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_right :
119	            𝒲.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒱.opens x) v).val
120	            = (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_right :
121	                𝒲.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒱.opens x)).op).hom v.val from rfl]
122	        rw [E2]
123	    _ = (X.unitsRestrict inf_le_left u).val * (X.unitsRestrict inf_le_right v).val
124	        * (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE _).op).hom (d₃.eqn x) := by
125	        rw [mul_assoc]
126	
127	/-- Structure extensionality for local-equation systems: the two `Prop` fields are
128	proof-irrelevant, so a system is determined by its cover and equations. -/
129	private lemma ext_eqn {d e : X.LocalEquations} (hcov : d.cover = e.cover)
130	    (heqn : d.eqn ≍ e.eqn) : d = e := by
131	  cases d; cases e
132	  cases hcov; cases heqn
133	  rfl
134	
135	/-- **Divisor equality preserves the Picard class** (`𝒪(D)` depends only on the divisor):
136	restrict both systems to the common refinement (`picClass_restrict`), where they differ
137	by a unit rescaling (`picClass_rescale`). -/
138	theorem picClass_eq_of_divEq {d₁ d₂ : X.LocalEquations} (h : DivEq d₁ d₂) :
139	    d₁.picClass = d₂.picClass := by
140	  obtain ⟨𝒲, h₁, h₂, H⟩ := h
141	  rw [← d₁.picClass_restrict 𝒲 h₁, ← d₂.picClass_restrict 𝒲 h₂]
142	  have hres : d₁.restrict 𝒲 h₁ = (d₂.restrict 𝒲 h₂).rescale (fun x => (H x).choose) := by
143	    refine ext_eqn rfl (heq_of_eq (funext fun x => ?_))
144	    exact (H x).choose_spec
145	  rw [hres, picClass_rescale]
146	
147	end Scheme.LocalEquations

151	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
152	variable (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
153	variable (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k)
154	
155	/-- **The `Fin`-indexed basic-open cover data** of the two pinned charts of the relative
156	curve (`informal/spec-dd-1.md` §1a): `m₀ + m₁` basic-open generators with partition
157	witnesses. The DAT-1 datum `BasicOpenCoverData` carries `Type u` index fields and hence
158	lives in `Type (u+1)`; this `Fin`-indexed form is the `Type u` carrier a functor value
159	can quotient. -/
160	structure FinCoverData [IsAffineHom π] : Type u where
161	  /-- The number of chart-0 pieces. -/
162	  m₀ : ℕ
163	  /-- The number of chart-1 pieces. -/
164	  m₁ : ℕ
165	  /-- The chart-0 basic-open generators. -/
166	  h₀ : Fin m₀ → Γ(relCurve C R, (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀)
167	  /-- The chart-1 basic-open generators. -/
168	  h₁ : Fin m₁ → Γ(relCurve C R, (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁)
169	  /-- The chart-0 partition coefficients. -/
170	  a₀ : Fin m₀ → Γ(relCurve C R, (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀)
171	  /-- The chart-1 partition coefficients. -/
172	  a₁ : Fin m₁ → Γ(relCurve C R, (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁)
173	  /-- The chart-0 partition witness. -/
174	  partition₀ : ∑ j : Fin m₀, a₀ j * h₀ j = 1
175	  /-- The chart-1 partition witness. -/
176	  partition₁ : ∑ j : Fin m₁, a₁ j * h₁ j = 1
177	
178	namespace FinCoverData
179	
180	variable {C R π} [IsAffineHom π] (D : FinCoverData C R π)
181	
182	/-- The gluing index of the adaptation, `Fin m₀ ⊕ Fin m₁`. -/
183	abbrev index : Type := Fin D.m₀ ⊕ Fin D.m₁
184	
185	/-- The pieces: the basic opens `D(h_j)` of the two pinned charts. -/
186	noncomputable def pieces : D.index → (relCurve C R).Opens :=
187	  Sum.elim (fun j => (relCurve C R).basicOpen (D.h₀ j))
188	    (fun j => (relCurve C R).basicOpen (D.h₁ j))
189	
190	@[simp]
191	lemma pieces_inl (j : Fin D.m₀) :
192	    D.pieces (Sum.inl j) = (relCurve C R).basicOpen (D.h₀ j) := rfl
193	
194	@[simp]
195	lemma pieces_inr (j : Fin D.m₁) :
196	    D.pieces (Sum.inr j) = (relCurve C R).basicOpen (D.h₁ j) := rfl
197	
198	/-- The chart-0 pieces cover the pinned chart `V₀ᴿ`. -/
199	lemma cover₀ : (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ ≤
200	    ⨆ j : Fin D.m₀, (relCurve C R).basicOpen (D.h₀ j) :=
201	  le_iSup_basicOpen_of_sum_eq_one D.a₀ D.h₀ D.partition₀
202	
203	/-- The chart-1 pieces cover the pinned chart `V₁ᴿ`. -/
204	lemma cover₁ : (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ ≤
205	    ⨆ j : Fin D.m₁, (relCurve C R).basicOpen (D.h₁ j) :=
206	  le_iSup_basicOpen_of_sum_eq_one D.a₁ D.h₁ D.partition₁
207	
208	end FinCoverData

210	/-- Restriction of sections of the relative curve as an `R`-algebra homomorphism
211	(`Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra` structures on both sides). -/
212	noncomputable def relResAlgHom {W V : (relCurve C R).Opens} (h : W ≤ V) :
213	    Γ(relCurve C R, V) →ₐ[R] Γ(relCurve C R, W) :=
214	  AlgHom.mk' (CommRingCat.Hom.hom ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE h).op))
215	    (fun c x => by
216	      simp only [Algebra.smul_def]
217	      rw [map_mul]
218	      congr 1
219	      rw [Scheme.algebraMap_overSectionsAlgebra, Scheme.algebraMap_overSectionsAlgebra]
220	      exact (relCurve C R).overAlgebraMap_apply_res R (homOfLE h).op c)
221	
222	@[simp]
223	lemma relResAlgHom_apply {W V : (relCurve C R).Opens} (h : W ≤ V) (s : Γ(relCurve C R, V)) :
224	    relResAlgHom C R h s = ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE h).op).hom s :=
225	  rfl
226	
227	/-- **The finite chart adaptation of a local-equation system** (worksheet §1.1 (D1)):
228	basic-open cover data of the two pinned charts, equations `f_j` on the pieces, and the
229	pointwise refinement clause `eqn_rel` — on the overlap of each piece with any member of
230	`d.cover`, `f_j` agrees with `d`'s equation up to a unit. Regularity of the `f_j` is
231	DERIVED (`DivisorAdaptation.eqn_regular`), not stored. -/
232	structure DivisorAdaptation [IsAffineHom π] (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations) :
233	    Type u extends FinCoverData C R π where
234	  /-- The equation on the piece `D(h_j)`. -/
235	  eqn : ∀ j : toFinCoverData.index, Γ(relCurve C R, toFinCoverData.pieces j)
236	  /-- The equations refine `d` pointwise up to units: on the overlap of each piece with
237	  any member of `d`'s cover, `f_j` and `d`'s equation differ by a unit. Point-free (the
238	  `DivEq` spelling), so it pulls back along arbitrary morphisms — the resolution of the
239	  DD-1 pt-transport seam (`informal/spec-dd-2.md` §1a). The quantifier ranges over ALL
240	  `y`: the empty overlap carries the zero ring, where the clause is trivial. -/
241	  eqn_rel : ∀ (j : toFinCoverData.index) (y : relCurve C R),
242	    ∃ u : Γ(relCurve C R, toFinCoverData.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y)ˣ,
243	      ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_left).op).hom (eqn j)
244	        = (u : Γ(relCurve C R, toFinCoverData.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y))
245	          * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_right).op).hom (d.eqn y)
246	
247	namespace DivisorAdaptation
248	
249	variable {C R π} [IsAffineHom π] {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
250	variable (A : DivisorAdaptation C R π d)
251	
252	/-- **The compatibility constructor from anchored refinement data** (the pre-DD-2 field
253	layout): a base point `pt j` of `d.cover` per piece with `pieces j ≤ d.cover.opens (pt j)`
254	and a comparison unit `eqn j = unit j · res (d.eqn (pt j))`. The pointwise clause
255	`eqn_rel` is derived by rewriting `d.eqn (pt j)` into `d.eqn y` through the transition
256	unit `d.ratioUnit (pt j) y` on the overlap (the `DivEq.trans` calc pattern). -/
257	def ofAnchors (D : FinCoverData C R π)
258	    (eqn : ∀ j : D.index, Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j))
259	    (pt : D.index → relCurve C R)
260	    (piece_le : ∀ j, D.pieces j ≤ d.cover.opens (pt j))
261	    (unit : ∀ j, Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j)ˣ)
262	    (eqn_eq : ∀ j, eqn j = (unit j : Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j))
263	      * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE (piece_le j)).op).hom (d.eqn (pt j))) :
264	    DivisorAdaptation C R π d where
265	  toFinCoverData := D
266	  eqn := eqn
267	  eqn_rel := fun j y => by
268	    have hWle : D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y
269	        ≤ d.cover.opens (pt j) ⊓ d.cover.opens y :=
270	      inf_le_inf (piece_le j) le_rfl
271	    have E1 := congrArg ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE
272	      (inf_le_left : D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y ≤ D.pieces j)).op).hom (eqn_eq j)
273	    rw [map_mul, Scheme.LocalEquations.res_res] at E1
274	    have E2 := congrArg ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE hWle).op).hom
275	      (d.eqn_restrict_eq (pt j) y)
276	    rw [map_mul, Scheme.LocalEquations.res_res, Scheme.LocalEquations.res_res] at E2
277	    refine ⟨(relCurve C R).unitsRestrict inf_le_left (unit j)
278	      * (relCurve C R).unitsRestrict hWle (d.ratioUnit (pt j) y), ?_⟩
279	    rw [Units.val_mul]
280	    calc ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_left).op).hom (eqn j)
281	        = ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict inf_le_left (unit j)).val
282	          * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE
283	              ((inf_le_left : D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y ≤ D.pieces j).trans
284	                (piece_le j))).op).hom (d.eqn (pt j)) := by
285	          rw [show ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict (inf_le_left :
286	              D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y ≤ D.pieces j) (unit j)).val
287	              = ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left :
288	                  D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y ≤ D.pieces j)).op).hom (unit j).val
289	            from rfl]
290	          exact E1
291	      _ = ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict inf_le_left (unit j)).val
292	          * (((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict hWle (d.ratioUnit (pt j) y)).val
293	            * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE (hWle.trans
294	                (inf_le_right : d.cover.opens (pt j) ⊓ d.cover.opens y
295	                  ≤ d.cover.opens y))).op).hom (d.eqn y)) := by
296	          rw [show ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict hWle (d.ratioUnit (pt j) y)).val
297	              = ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map
298	                  (homOfLE hWle).op).hom (d.ratioUnit (pt j) y).val from rfl]
299	          rw [E2]
300	      _ = ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict inf_le_left (unit j)).val
301	          * ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict hWle (d.ratioUnit (pt j) y)).val
302	          * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE
303	              (inf_le_right : D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y
304	                ≤ d.cover.opens y)).op).hom (d.eqn y) := by
305	          rw [mul_assoc]
306	
307	/-- The adaptation's equations are regular: at `z ∈ D(h_j)` the pointwise clause
308	`eqn_rel j z` presents the germ of `f_j` as a unit germ times the germ of `d`'s regular
309	equation at the member of `z` itself. -/
310	theorem eqn_regular (j : A.index) (z : relCurve C R) (hz : z ∈ A.pieces j) :
311	    ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (A.pieces j) z hz).hom (A.eqn j)
312	      ∈ nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C R).presheaf.stalk z) := by
313	  obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := A.eqn_rel j z
314	  have hzW : z ∈ A.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z := ⟨hz, d.cover.mem_opens z⟩
315	  have hgerm : ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (A.pieces j) z hz).hom (A.eqn j)
316	      = ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (A.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z) z hzW).hom
317	          (u : Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z))
318	        * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (d.cover.opens z) z
319	            (d.cover.mem_opens z)).hom (d.eqn z) := by
320	    have h := congrArg ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ
321	      (A.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z) z hzW).hom hu
322	    rw [map_mul, TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply, TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply] at h
323	    exact h
324	  rw [hgerm]
325	  exact mul_mem
326	    ((u.isUnit.map ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ
327	      (A.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z) z hzW).hom).mem_nonZeroDivisors)
328	    (d.regular z z (d.cover.mem_opens z))
